question: Which of the following is NOT a possible isomer of hexane?
solution:
The correct answer is __**option 3**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 3: 2-ethyl pentane** is not a possible isomer of hexane.
 
• Hexane (C₆H₁₄) has several isomers, including different structural forms such as straight-chain and branched-chain alkanes.
 
• Possible isomers of hexane include n-hexane, 2-methyl pentane, 3-methyl pentane, 2,2-dimethyl butane, and 2,3-dimethyl butane.
 
• **2-ethyl pentane** is not a valid isomer because it would imply a seven-carbon chain, which does not match the molecular formula of hexane.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Isomers are compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulas.
 
• Structural isomers differ in the connectivity of their atoms, while stereoisomers differ in the spatial arrangement of atoms.
 
• Hexane's structural isomers include different arrangements of the carbon atoms, leading to variations in the branching of the carbon chain.
